hero.label: My public IP
hero.errorHint: Check your network connection or whether an ad blocker is blocking the request, then try again. Browser info below is still available.
hero.v4Note: You connected to this site over IPv4. If your network also has IPv6, the browser picks one of them, so only one address is visible at a time.
hero.v6Note: You connected to this site over IPv6. Your IPv4 address uses a separate path and is not visible here. The WebRTC check below may reveal the other version.

loc.accuracy: IP location reflects where the ISP assigned the address and may be tens of km or more off, or even show a different city.

net.note: All values are what the Cloudflare edge serving this site sees. No third-party IP lookup API is used.

vpnHint.title: Possible VPN or proxy
vpnHint.body: Your browser time zone {browser} differs from the IP location time zone {ip}. You may be using a VPN, proxy or roaming, or the IP location data may be inaccurate.

webrtc.title: WebRTC IP leak test
webrtc.desc: Checks whether WebRTC (used for video calls and P2P) bypasses your VPN and reveals your real IP. Pressing the button sends one request to Cloudflare's public STUN server (stun.cloudflare.com).
webrtc.unsupported: WebRTC is unavailable or disabled in this browser, so it cannot leak your IP.
webrtc.blocked: The WebRTC test was blocked (browser setting or extension). Leak risk is low.
webrtc.mdnsOk: Your local IP is hidden behind a random .local name (mDNS). This is the default protection in modern browsers; your private IP is not exposed.
webrtc.localExposed: Your local (private) IP is exposed: {ips}. You can block WebRTC local IP exposure in browser settings or with an extension.
webrtc.leak: WebRTC shows a different address from your public IP above: {ips}. If you are on a VPN, WebRTC may be bypassing it.
webrtc.same: The public IP seen via WebRTC matches your public IP above. No extra leak through this path.
webrtc.otherVersion: A public address of the other IP version is visible: {ips}. Normal on dual-stack (IPv4+IPv6) networks; a leak if your VPN tunnels only one version.
webrtc.noStun: No STUN response. Your network may block UDP or the browser restricts WebRTC public IP exposure.
webrtc.note: Web pages cannot reliably see your private IP because of mDNS protection. Check it with ipconfig on Windows or ifconfig / ip addr on macOS and Linux.

check.title: IP address check
check.desc: Instantly check whether another IP address is valid and which range it belongs to. Leave empty to check your own IP.
check.label: IP address

explain.public: Globally routable on the internet. Firewall allowlists use addresses like this.
explain.private: Used only inside home or office networks (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16); not directly reachable from outside.
explain.loopback: Points to the machine itself (127.0.0.1, ::1). Used for local development servers.
explain.linkLocal: Auto-assigned when DHCP fails (169.254.x.x) or used only on the local link in IPv6 (fe80::).
explain.cgnat: Range ISPs use to share one public IP among many subscribers (100.64/10). Port forwarding is hard behind it.
explain.uniqueLocal: IPv6 private addresses (fc00::/7), not routed on the internet.
explain.multicast: Group address for sending to many receivers at once; not assigned to a device.
explain.reserved: Reserved for special purposes (0.0.0.0, 240/4, documentation 2001:db8::, etc.) and not normally used.

ipChecker.title: IP Address Checker
ipChecker.description: Check your public IP address, location, ISP, and network information at a glance.

whatIsIp.title: What is an IP Address?
items: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a unique identifier for devices connected to the internet
Public IP is the address visible externally, while private IP is the internal network address
There are two formats: IPv4 (e.g., 192.168.0.1) and IPv6 (e.g., 2001:db8::1)

whyCheck.title: When to Check Your IP
items: When setting up remote access or server configuration

whatIs.title: What is the IP Address Checker?
whatIs.description: A tool that instantly displays your public IP address along with geolocation data (country, city), ISP, ASN, and timezone — all in one place. Commonly used to verify VPN connectivity, check which region a streaming or gaming service sees you as, and quickly retrieve your IP for firewall whitelist configurations.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Your current public IP (IPv4 or IPv6) appears in the blue card as soon as the page opens. Copy it with the button next to it.
2. The location and network cards show country/city, ISP (ASN), the Cloudflare data center you hit, and HTTP/TLS versions.
3. Turn on your VPN and press Refresh to see the new IP and location, then run the WebRTC leak test to check for VPN bypass.
4. Enter another address in 'IP address check' to instantly see if it is valid, IPv4/IPv6, and private/public/CGNAT.
5. Press 'Copy all' to copy every item as text for support tickets or firewall requests.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: When using a VPN or proxy, this tool lets you instantly verify whether your IP has changed and whether you are connected from the intended country.
Useful for checking which country a service thinks you are connecting from when using a VPN or roaming abroad. Bypassing region restrictions may violate a service's terms of use.
Quickly copy your public IP for server configs, firewall rules, or remote access setups that require a fixed IP whitelist.

items.q: Does the IP location reveal my home address?
items.a: No. IP-based geolocation shows the region where your ISP has assigned that IP block, not your physical address. Accuracy is usually at the city level, and some connections such as mobile data may even show a different city.

items.q: Will I see an IPv4 or IPv6 address?
items.a: Depending on your device and network setup, either IPv4 (e.g., 123.45.67.89) or IPv6 (e.g., 2001:db8::1) may be shown. Both versions are supported; the address displayed corresponds to the protocol used for the connection.

items.q: Will my IP look different on a corporate or school Wi-Fi?
items.a: Yes. Corporate and school networks use NAT, so all devices on the network share a single public IP. This tool will show the network's public IP, not your device's private IP.
